enhancing model capabilities. We release our resources at the STILL project

In this report, we present the third technical report on the development of slow-
thinking models as part of the STILL project. As the technical pathway becomes
clearer, scaling RL training has become a central technique for implementing
such reasoning models. We systematically experiment with and document the
effects of various factors influencing RL training, conducting experiments on
both base models and fine-tuned models. Specifically, we demonstrate that our
RL training approach consistently improves the QWEN2.5-32B base models,
enhancing both response length and test accuracy. Furthermore, we show that even
when a model like DEEPSEEK-R1-DISTILL-QWEN-1.5B has already achieved a
high performance level, it can be further refined through RL training, reaching an
accuracy of 39.33% on AIME 2024. Beyond RL training, we also explore the use
of tool manipulation, finding that it significantly boosts the reasoning performance
of large reasoning models. This approach achieves a remarkable accuracy of
86.67% with greedy search on AIME 2024, underscoring its effectiveness in
enhancing model capabilities. We release our resources at the STILL project
website: https://github.com/RUCAIBox/Slow_Thinking_with_LLMs.
